title: False Bottom
genre: Canterbury-scene jazz-rock pop (Soft Machine and Caravan lineage)
subject: A stage magician's assistant who spends every show folded into the false bottom of a trunk, counting the audience's applause from inside, decides tonight that she will take the bow before him, because the trick only works on her cue.
caption: Canterbury-scene jazz-rock pop, fluid 7/8 verses opening into straight 4/4 choruses. Warm Fender Rhodes electric piano with chromatic chord movement, a fuzz-toned electric bass playing winding melodic lines, a soprano saxophone doubling the vocal melody and trading phrases, a busy jazz drum kit with ride cymbal and snare ghost notes. Dry English 1971 studio texture, slightly woolly warm tape, Rhodes and bass forward. Female lead, plain warm alto, mid register, conversational and deadpan delivery with clean unison harmony on the hook. Clear full voice, every word enunciated, steady sung melody on every line. 126 BPM, E minor. Dry, wry, quietly triumphant. No synth pads, no trap drums, no autotune, no big pop drops, no stadium guitar solos.
lyrics:
[Intro - Rhodes and fuzz bass in 7/8, soprano sax enters]

[Verse 1]
I fold myself in at a quarter past nine
Knees to my chin in the lining
The velvet smells of dust and pine
I count the hands outside it

[Chorus]
False bottom, false bottom
Who's the one who makes it work
Four hundred hands above my head
And he gets to take the bow

[Verse 2]
Two taps for the card, three for the dove
One slow knock for the cue
He's waited on my hand six years
And never thanked the trunk

[Pre-Chorus]
The rabbit has his own dressing room
I get a hook and a hood
Tonight I'll let the lid go slow
And let him count the wood

[Chorus]
False bottom, false bottom
Tonight I know the way
The lid goes up when I say so
And he can wait for my cue

[Bridge - sax solo over Rhodes, groove tightens to 4/4]
The lid goes up and I stand
With the whole room in my hands

[Outro - soprano sax and Rhodes in 7/8]
Two taps for the card
One slow bow for me
